notes: FALL TEST (reported separately for the coordinator): not triggered. After removing every evaluated row with an extra at DINOv2 cosine >= 0.75 the gains are +0.305 (PlantDoc, 0.246 to 0.361, threshold 0.145) and +0.272 (PlantSeg, 0.199 to 0.347, threshold 0.117); intervals stay far from zero. Weakest slice: PlantSeg rows that do have a neighbour, +0.147 (0.072 to 0.239). SAFETY READ (separate): a small but real worsening, moderate confidence (about 65%) that it is not a blocker. On the seen rows sick plants called some healthy class went from 8 to 27 of 822 (1.0% to 3.3%); of those, 17 are the same plant's healthy class. At E5's threshold only 2 E12 rows would be shown as a confident healthy answer (0 for E4), but E5 was calibrated on E4 and E12's mistaken healthy rows are more confident (mean 0.58 vs 0.41), so a refit would be needed. On held-out rows E12 is clearly safer (PlantSeg sick-called-healthy 18.9% to 3.3%, PlantDoc healthy called sick 82% to 4%). The web page shows a green check and 'Healthy' for any answered healthy label with no caveat, and answer.py has no healthy-specific wording, so a wrong healthy answer reads as reassurance; that is a product risk that exists for E4 as well. Rule caveats: one seed per model; seen-source difference +0.012 with an interval spanning zero is only noise-sized; E12 used 2 loader workers vs 4, the augmentation stream differs. How far the held-out gain generalises: the extras, PlantDoc and PlantSeg are all web photos (shared stock-photo sites and captions are visible in the montages), so the held-out gain is web-to-web transfer, mostly web healthy leaves for PlantDoc (healthy accuracy 0.10 to 0.71, sick only 0.61 to 0.64); it says little about new phone photos in the garden, and field_test has not been used. T4.5's copy filter drops extras at cosine >= 0.80 against field_dev, which also removes the nearest neighbours of the evaluated rows, if anything making the held-out numbers conservative on this axis. YOUR READ / RECOMMENDATION: do not replace E4's model with E12's on this evidence alone; the rule said keep E4 and the seen-source gain is not distinguishable from zero. The held-out gain is real in the sense of not being a near-copy artefact, but it is the right kind of result for web photos and mostly shows E4's held-out arm lacked web healthy examples, so it does not show the E12 model is better on the phone photos the app will see. It would change if: a second seed (and 4 workers) reproduces the seen result and held-out gain, E5's calibration refit on E12 keeps sick-called-healthy answers at or below E4's, and a small set of real phone photos (not web) shows no loss; that decision belongs to the person, must be recorded as made after seeing these numbers, and then E5 is refit on E12 with its probabilities file.
